newsitem.title: USA: Archer will work with Clinton on Social Security.
newsitem.headline: Archer will work with Clinton on Social Security.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said Monday he was willing to work with President Clinton to find a long-term solution to Social Security's financial problems.

The Texas Republican said his committee would hold hearings on a new report issued by a divided Social Security advisory commission, that suggested some portion of the Social Security payroll tax should be invested in private markets.
House Majority Leader Dick Armey also issued a statement praising the panel's recommendation to invest part of Social Security payroll taxes in the private market.

"When a nonpartisan commission ... endorses turning to the private sector to ensure the solvency of Social Security, we must acknowledge a vast paradigm shift on the issue," Armey said in a statement.
"Clearly the vital center in the public policy debate has moved from a belief in greater government to a belief in market-based solutions," he said.
Earlier, Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, said the panel's findings made it more likely Congress would act on the issue of privatization.

The 13-member Social Security panel was unable to agree on a plan for ensuring the long-term solvency of the federal retirement program. It did agree that some Social Security payroll taxes should be invested in the private markets.

Recommendations ranged from having the federal government investment about 40 percent of the trust fund in stocks, bonds and other investment instruments, to setting up a two-tiered system and letting individuals decide how to invest part of their payroll taxes.

Archer, whose committee oversees Social Security, said despite the panel's division, there was agreement something "new and structural must be done to modernize our nation's most important pension system."
Archer also said he was looking to see what changes Clinton recommended in the Medicare health care program for the elderly in the budget he will submit to Congress.

"I will look to the specific Medicare changes recommended in the president's upcoming budget as a signal of how willing he is to take the lead in solving the growing, structrual crises in our nation's retirement programs," Archer said.
